tabānus, tabānī m.

noun, second declension

a horsefly, gadfly

Lewis & Short: also called asīlus.

Other words

  • asīlus, asīlī m. — gadfly, horsefly

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 3.147 (Lewis & Short)

    The old Roman name, already out of use in Seneca’s time (Ep. 58); the usual word is tabānus (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Tabānī bombilant.

    Horseflies buzz.Traupman 329

  • cui nōmen asīlō Rōmānum est

    whose Roman name is asilusVerg. G. 3.147–148

See also fly.
